text:
matt: Posting a short proposal for request/response logging + sampling + PII redaction. TL;DR: do deterministic edge redaction, route-level sampling, and store schema-only artifacts for analytics. Thoughts?

anya: Agree we need deterministic masking at the edge. If any plaintext PII leaves the customer boundary we lose compliance guarantees. Edge redaction = must.

raj: Only concern is CPU cost at edge for heavy regexes. If we run full redaction on every request it might add latency for hot routes. Can we do a fast-path + heavier scrub for sampled items?

kelsey: I don't love sampling before redaction (raj's idea) because that means some raw PII could be persisted if sampling picks a request and we postpone redaction downstream. If we sample after redaction we avoid that risk. Edge redaction + route sampling seems safer.

matt: Good point. Proposal update: 1) edge redaction fast-path using token-based rules + small regex whitelist for obvious patterns; 2) route-level sample_rate (default 0.01) applied after redaction; 3) sampled items get full structured payload stored in analytics index with schema versioning.

anya: Example of fast-path redaction pseudocode I discussed with infra: ```
// pseudo
redact(text):
  for token in simple_tokens(text):
    if looks_like_email(token): replace_with("<email:HASH>")
  apply small set of regexes for cc/ssn/phone
  return text
```

raj: That helps. Also we should include deterministic hashing for customer ids and user ids so we can join events without storing raw identifiers. Use HMAC with per-customer salt kept in KMS.

kelsey: +1 on HMAC approach. Also we must support header-driven sampling overrides for customers running evals: X-Redwood-Log: full. That should be gated by account-level entitlements.

telemetry-bot: NOTE: sampling affects metrics fidelity. If route-level default is 1%, we need to emit sampling_ratio in every log event so downstream analytics can correctly weight aggregates.

matt: Agreed. Stored event schema should include: redaction_version, sampling_ratio, sample_seed, hashed_ids, route, model, latency_ms. Example stored JSON (post-redaction): ```
{
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "model": "open-llama-1b",
  "prompt_snippet": "<prompt:HASH>",
  "response_shape": { "tokens": 42, "sampler": "top_p" },
  "hashed_user_id": "hmac-v1:abc123",
  "sampling_ratio": 0.01,
  "redaction_version": "r2"
}
```

anya: We should also make sure telemetry events include a boolean `contains_suspected_pii` for flagged heuristics. That triggers a security review workflow if true AND sampling decided to persist.

raj: On GDPR right-to-erasure: because we store hashed ids, we need a mapping per-customer to resolve and delete. Plan: maintain per-customer salt + an opt-out/erase API that rotates the salt so previously hashed ids become unresolvable. This avoids storing a direct lookup table.

kelsey: We also need retention TTLs by account tier. Default 30 days for sampled payloads, 90 days for enterprise with opt-in. Make retention configurable from Console. Expose per-route retention overrides.

matt: Rollout plan suggestion: 1) feature flag behind `edge-redaction-v2` 2) default sampling 1% on non-prod routes 3) enable enterprise full-log header only for opted accounts 4) gradually increase redaction ruleset with telemetry.

raj: Perf test checklist: benchmark redaction fast-path on 95th percentile request size, measure p50/p95 added latency, and memory overhead. If >10ms p95 we need to move some regex work to async scrubber before storage.

kelsey: UX: in Console, add Logs -> Sampling page showing per-route sample_rate, last sample id, and ability to request a replay of a sampled event (redacted) for 7 days. Must ensure replay permission checks.

telemetry-bot: DEPLOY NOTE: config change to enable `edge-redaction-v2` will create new log schema. Consumers: please support `redaction_version` parity.

deploy-bot: deploy started for `edge-redaction-v2` in staging (build 2026.03.18-1123).

matt: Action items: - I will open RFC with the redaction ruleset + schema example. - @raj to run perf tests and post numbers. - @kelsey to draft Console UI wires for sampling + retention. - @anya to coordinate sec review on regex rules.

anya: Sounds good. One more note: we should add strict deny-lists for obvious tokens (private keys, full credit card numbers) at the edge — those must never be persisted even in hashed form.

matt: Agreed. I'll add deny-list enforcement to the RFC. Thanks all :thumbsup:
